bib.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
bib.venue: Proceedings of EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019, pp. 3982-3992, Hong Kong

question: Can BERT/RoBERTa be fine-tuned with siamese and triplet networks to give fixed-size sentence embeddings usable with cosine similarity, avoiding the cross-encoder's quadratic cost?
hypothesis: Raw BERT outputs (mean or CLS) are poor sentence embeddings, but siamese fine-tuning on NLI data makes them semantically meaningful for cosine comparison.
contributions: SBERT: BERT/RoBERTa with pooling in siamese/triplet networks producing cosine-comparable sentence embeddings
State-of-the-art on STS and SentEval transfer vs InferSent and USE
Ablation of pooling and concatenation; speed comparison

method.summary: A pooling layer is added on top of BERT/RoBERTa and the network is fine-tuned in a siamese (tied weights) setup with classification, regression or triplet objectives. Default training is a 3-way softmax on SNLI+MultiNLI for one epoch; at inference only the embeddings and cosine similarity are used.

models.name: SBERT (BERT-base, BERT-large)

training.objective: Classification: cross-entropy on softmax(Wt(u,v,|u-v|)); regression: MSE on cosine(u,v); triplet: max(||sa-sp|| - ||sa-sn|| + eps, 0), Euclidean, eps = 1
training.epochs: 1 (NLI and WikiSec triplets); 4 for BERT cross-encoder on STSb (Table 2 caption); STSb epochs for SBERT not stated
training.wall_clock: SBERT can be tuned in less than 20 minutes
training.seeds: 10 random seeds for STSb and ablations

parameters.similarity: cosine; Manhattan and Euclidean gave roughly the same results

other.smart_batching: group similar-length sentences, pad to longest in mini-batch

limits: Cross-topic AFS: SBERT is about 7 points Spearman below BERT; authors say it may need more than two training topics.
Cross-encoder BERT beats SBERT on STSb when both are trained on STS (88.33 vs 85.35 base).
Authors say SBERT is not meant for transfer learning; fine-tuning BERT is more suitable.
On CPU SBERT is slower than InferSent; USE beats SBERT on SICK-R and TREC.
Training hyperparameters for STSb/AFS fine-tuning not given; no model sizes in parameters; no significance tests; XLNet tried but not reported.
